'''''Eucalyptus badjensis''''', commonly known as the '''Big Badja gum''',<ref name="CANBR" /> is a tree that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to south-eastern [[New South Wales]]. It has hard, rough bark on the lower part of the trunk, smooth grey bark above, often hanging in strips on the upper branches, linear to narrow lance-shaped, often curved adult leaves, green to yellow buds in groups of three in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s, white flowers and conical or bell-shaped fruit.[[File:Eucalyptus badjensis buds.jpg|thumb|225px|flower buds (leaves removed)]][[File:Eucalyptus badjensis fruit.jpg|thumb|225px|fruit]][[File:Eucalyptus badjensis bark.jpg|thumb|225px|bark]]

==Description==
''Eucalyptus badjensis'' is a tree that grows to a height of {{convert|45|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} and has hard, rough, greyish brown bark near the base of the trunk and smooth grey, green to light brownish or grey bark on the branches and upper part of the trunk. The upper bark is often shed in ribbons. The leaves on young plants and [[coppice]] regrowth are lance-shaped, {{convert|35-80|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long, {{convert|8-20|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide and lack a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. The adult leaves are linear to narrow lance-shaped, {{convert|85-200|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|10-20|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide on a petiole {{convert|6-14|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long. They are the same dull green colour on both surfaces. The flower buds are arranged in groups of three in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s on an unbranched [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] {{convert|3-4|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, the individual buds on a [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] up to {{convert|2|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long. The mature buds are oval, green to yellow, {{convert|4-5|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3-4|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide with a conical [[Operculum (botany)|operculum]]. Flowering occurs in January and the flowers are white. The fruit is a conical or bell-shaped [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{convert|3-5|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|4-6|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide on a pedicel up to {{convert|2|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="CANBR">{{cite web |title=''Eucalyptus badjensis'' Big Badja gum|url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/euclid/text/entities/eucalyptus_badjensis.htm?zoom_highlight=Eucalyptus+badjensis|publisher=Euclid: Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research |access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Ken |title=''Eucalyptus badjensis'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Eucalyptus~badjensis |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Chippendale |first1=George McCartney |title=''Eucalyptus badjensis'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Eucalyptus%20badjensis |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of the Environment and Energy, Canberra |access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref><ref name=Brooker>{{cite book|last1=Brooker|first1=M.I.H.|last2=Kleinig|first2=D.A.|title=Field Guide to Eucalypts (Volume 1: South-eastern Australia)|date=2006|publisher=Bloomings Books|location=Melbourne|isbn=1-876473-52-5|page=182|edition=3}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Eucalyptus badjensis'' was first formally described in 1924 by [[Wilfred Alexander Watt de Beuzeville|Wilfred de Beuzeville]] and [[Marcus Baldwin Welch|Marcus Welch]] "at an elevation of about 4,000 feet, three miles south of the [[Big Badja Hill|Big Badja Mountain]]". The description was published in ''[[Royal Society of New South Wales|Journal and Proceedings of the Royal Society of New South Wales]]''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus badjensis''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/454503 |publisher=APNI|access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="NSW">{{cite journal |last1=de Beuzeville |first1=Wilfred A.W. |last2=Welch |first2=Marcus B. |title=New species of ''Eucalyptus'' from southern New South Wales |journal=Journal and Proceedings of the Royal Society of New South Wales |date=1924 |volume=58 |pages=177–181 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/174132#page/209/mode/1up |access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref> The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''badjensis'') is a reference to the distribution of this eucalypt. The ending ''-ensis'' is a [[Latin]] [[wikt:suffix|suffix]] "denoting place, locality [or] country".<ref name="CANBR" /><ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.|page=303}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Big Badja gum is found in wet forest, on hills and plateaus on the eastern side of the [[Southern Tablelands]] in New South Wales. It grows in soils that are relatively fertile and where the rainfall is high and occurs from Big Badja Hill to [[Cathcart, New South Wales|Cathcart]] and [[Brown Mountain, New South Wales|Brown Mountain]], west of [[Bega, New South Wales|Bega]].<ref name="CANBR" /><ref name="RBGS" /><ref>A Field Guide to Eucalypts - Brooker & Kleinig volume 1, {{ISBN|0-909605-62-9}} page 216</ref>
